lines: Laughter and the smell of stew drift through the door of the {Ember & Oak}.
A neat little door with a brass knocker shaped like a leaf. Nobody answers.
The door is latched. Somewhere inside, a kettle begins to sing.
Fresh bread cools on the sill. You resist. Barely.
Split firewood is stacked high against the wall. Someone inside is humming a song about axes.
The barn smells of hay and patience. A cow regards you with polite indifference.
The well is deep and cold. Far below, something glints — a copper coin, wished upon long ago.
You make a small wish of your own.

text.speaker: Signpost
lines: Someone has added, in smaller letters: "They are not as friendly as they look."

text.speaker: Signpost
lines: {Amberleaf Grove}. Please do not feed the fireflies.

text.speaker: Signpost
lines: {Windmill Hill}. On a clear evening you can see the whole valley from here — and, some say, a little of tomorrow.

objects.name: Elder Maren
dialogue: Ah, a traveler. Welcome to {Emberfall}, child. Mind the cobbles — they are older than I am, and twice as stubborn.
Our founders followed this river up from the lowlands four hundred years ago. At dusk the falls catch the last of the sun and glow like embers in a hearth.
Hence the name. We are not an imaginative people, but we are an honest one.
If your feet are weary, the {Ember & Oak} has a bed and a bowl of stew. Rosalind keeps the hearth warm and the gossip warmer.

objects.name: Rosalind
dialogue: Welcome to the {Ember & Oak}! Warm beds, hot stew, and only a modest amount of snoring from the loft.

objects.name: Bertram
dialogue: Step right up! The finest produce this side of the river — and the only produce this side of the river, but let us not dwell on that.

dialogue.text: An apple, fresh from the valley orchards? For a new face in {Emberfall}, it is on the house.

objects.name: Corporal Hale
dialogue: Halt! State your— ah. Forgive me, traveler. Force of habit.
Nothing has crossed this bridge in years but ducks and gossip, and I have yet to arrest either.
The grove beyond turns to amber this time of year. Keep to the path after dark — the river is gentle, but she is deeper than she looks.

1AB077D988BD9A411607DAB3F6A469EF

objects.name: Old Tobin
dialogue: Hm? Oh, don't mind me. Just asking the turnips how they are getting on.
Soil's been kind this year. Rain came when we asked for it and kept away when we didn't. Can't ask fairer than that.
If you see my granddaughter, tell her the chickens have filed a formal complaint.
FA0AD15A9AD25CBAA2F2092AED9B62CE
7432D08932A6C1BD5D8F9FBDA3DD4EDE

objects.name: Pip
dialogue: Shh! I'm sneaking up on {Duchess}. She's the plump one. She's also the fastest, which is not fair at all.
Grandpa says if I catch her, I get to name the next batch of eggs!

objects.name: Wren
dialogue: A listener! Sit, sit. The fire is warm and my lute is — mostly — in tune.
This one is called {Emberfall Evening}. I wrote it on that very bench, the night the falls turned gold.
33392DF2B1046E5A355D67CAFDDB4D80

objects.name: Ottoline Quill
dialogue: Oh! A visitor on the hill. I am cataloguing how the light moves over this valley. Would you believe it is different every hour?
Press {T} and watch the day turn — dawn, noon, golden hour, dusk and night. I have documented each one. Twice.
{R} summons the weather: rain, then snow, then clear skies again. Do not ask me how. Scholarship has its limits.
{P} hides everything but the view. {Q} and {E} turn the world around you, and {Z} and {X} — or the wheel — bring it closer or push it away.
And should you wish to see my working notes, {~} opens them. {H} will remind you of all this, should you forget.
